newsitem.title: USA: Bondholders dismissed from Ill. incinerator case.
newsitem.headline: Bondholders dismissed from Ill. incinerator case.

text.p: A Cook County, Ill., Circuit Court judge on Monday dismissed a complaint brought against the state of Illinois by holders of incinerator bonds.
Judge Edwin Berman ruled bondholders had no standing to bring the lawsuit, which was filed as part of a lawsuit originally brought by the developers of two bond-financed incinerators.

The lawsuit raised legal and constitutional questions about the state's removal of a subsidy for two waste-to-energy incinerators that were approved by the state and financed with unrated, tax-exempt bonds.

However, Berman did not completely dismiss the developer's part of the lawsuit, according to his clerk. He declined to dismiss one count alleged by developers, CGE Ford Heights and CGE Fulton, that dealt with the legality of the retroactive removal of the state subsidy. Instead he ordered the developers to more fully brief their allegation, the clerk said.
In August, Berman had denied a motion by lawyers representing the Illinois Commerce Commission, one of the defendants in the case, to receive more information on the count from the developers.

Berman also kept alive two other counts the developers lodged against Commonwealth Edison Co., the utility that was to purchase electricity from the incinerators at a higher rate subsidized by the state.
The judge granted the state's motion to dismiss one claim that alleged the Illinois General Assembly violated legislative procedures in amending the Retail Rate Act in January.
CGE Ford Heights filed the lawsuit shortly after Gov. Jim Edgar in March signed the amendment into law.
Lawyers representing the developers, bondholders and the state commerce commission were not immediately available to comment on Berman's ruling.
The Illinois Development Finance Authority sold $79.5 million of bonds for the Ford Heights project in 1994 and Fulton sold $84.6 million of bonds for an incinerator last December.

While awaiting the outcome of its lawsuit, CGE Ford Heights filed for bankruptcy earlier this year. In May, a federal bankruptcy court judge in Wilmington, Del. approved an agreement between the developer and bondholders to make interest payments only on the bonds until Oct. 1, 1997.
